History_of_Present_Illness.content: Diarrhoea for 3 days, initially watery and now very loose
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Diarrhoea x3 days; initially watery → now very loose

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Diarrhoea frequency is high, patient has lost count, with at least 4 episodes today
Subjective fever with descriptions of serious temperature and feeling boiling, no thermometer reading available
Vomiting everything including water and tea
Last episode of vomiting was approximately 2 hours ago after breakfast
Periumbilical abdominal pain located at the navel, very tender to touch
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Abdo pain: periumbilical/at navel; very tender to touch

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Abdominal pain is colicky, comes and goes, and is associated with an urge to open bowels
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: colicky/comes & goes; assoc urge to open bowels

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Passing urine is normal with last urination about 1 hour ago
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: GU: passing urine OK; last urination ~1 hr ago

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Baseline bowel habit is normally once daily in the morning without usual diarrhoea or constipation
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Baseline bowels: normally daily AM, once/day; no usual diarrhoea/constipation

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Has sick contact with brother who has similar symptoms
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Sick contact: brother w/ similar sx

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Reports that many people at school have similar illness and patient has been in contact
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: “everyone in school’s got this”; pt has been in contact

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Tried oral rehydration solution made with salt and sugar about three times per day for two days without benefit due to vomiting
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Tried: ORS (salt/sugar mix) ~3x/day x2 days; not helping due to vomiting

Past_Medical_History.content: No prior abdominal problems aside from menstrual cramps
Past_Medical_History.source_text: No prior abdo problems (aside from menstrual cramps)

Medications.content: Uses ibuprofen as needed for menstrual cramps
Has been taking oral rehydration solution about three times per day for two days

Social_and_Family_History.content: Working from home today due to symptoms
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: working from home today due to sx

Social_and_Family_History.content: Drinks alcohol occasionally, about a pint
Last menstrual period was approximately 2 weeks ago

Assessment.content: Acute gastroenteritis, possibly viral or foodborne, with consideration of bacterial cause given persistent symptoms for 3 days, associated with diarrhea, vomiting, subjective fever, and sick contact
Assessment.source_text: 1. Acute gastroenteritis (viral vs foodborne; consider bacterial given persistent sx x3 days) w/ diarrhea, vomiting, subjective fever; sick contact.

Assessment.content: At risk of dehydration due to inability to keep fluids down, though still urinating with last urination 1 hour ago
Assessment.source_text: 2. Dehydration risk d/t inability to keep fluids down (still urinating; last 1 hr ago).

Plan_of_Care.content: Arrange urgent clinic appointment for stool sample to be sent as soon as possible
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Urgent clinic appt for stool sample; send ASAP

Plan_of_Care.content: Advise supportive diet with simple foods such as toast or biscuit and avoidance of fruit, vegetables, and milk
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Supportive diet: simple foods (toast/biscuit); avoid fruit/veg/milk

Plan_of_Care.content: Continue oral rehydration solution with tiny frequent sips taken constantly
Clinic review planned to assess hydration status
If symptoms worsen or patient feels more unwell, seek urgent assessment in A&E and call back if needed
Plan_of_Care.source_text: If worsening/more unwell → urgent assessment in A&E; call back if needed

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient to book appointment via support line
